claims.text: Controlled pre-oxidation will form a thin alumina (Al2O3) scale on boride-based components.
The pre-oxidation treatment will improve resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion relative to untreated components.
The alumina scale will function as a stable diffusion barrier.
The proposed pre-oxidation treatment induces in-situ formation of an adherent alumina scale.
Typical hot-dip aluminum-plating exposure occurs at approximately 650°C.
The protective alumina scale can remain intact and adherent during thermal cycling and repeated immersion in molten aluminum.
Pre-oxidation produces a continuous, dense, and chemically inert alumina surface scale.
The alumina scale prevents direct contact between molten aluminum and the boride substrate.
The alumina scale limits interdiffusion between the molten aluminum and the substrate.
The alumina scale limits reactive wetting by molten aluminum.
Limiting direct contact, interdiffusion, and reactive wetting reduces the corrosion rate.
Pre-oxidized components will exhibit lower weight loss than untreated components under identical molten-aluminum exposure.
Pre-oxidized components will exhibit less surface degradation than untreated components under identical molten-aluminum exposure.
Untreated boride-based components typically have higher corrosion rates in molten aluminum.
Protection depends on formation of a uniform and well-adherent alumina scale.
Deviations in oxidation temperature, duration, or oxygen concentration may diminish the protective effect.
Extreme operational stresses may diminish the protective effect.
The alumina scale's long-term stability and uniformity under prolonged cyclic thermal and mechanical stresses are uncertain.
